section.title: Overview
section.para: Since 3.0.0, an application that uses the built-in OpenNLP components and loads its models from files or streams can be compiled into a GraalVM native image without any OpenNLP specific configuration. The OpenNLP jars ship the metadata the image builder needs, and the code paths a model takes at load time do not use reflection:

listitem.para: Tool factories, artifact serializers, feature generator factories, sequence codecs, trainers and model readers are referenced by class name in model manifests, feature descriptors and training parameters. Each OpenNLP module registers its implementations through an ExtensionRegistrar service, and ExtensionLoader creates a registered extension through its registered supplier. See .

Bundled resources that are read by a name computed at run time, for instance the stopword list of a language, are listed in META-INF/native-image/org.apache.opennlp/<artifactId>/reachability-metadata.json of the jar that bundles them. The image builder picks these files up automatically.

section.para: This covers opennlp-api, opennlp-runtime, the opennlp-ml-* modules without opennlp-dl, opennlp-model-resolver and opennlp-formats. The image is verified in the project's CI with a smoke test that runs sentence detection, tokenization, POS tagging and name finding on models loaded from files; the source of that test, the opennlp-native-tests module, is a minimal example of a native OpenNLP application.
The runtime also registers DependencyModel with ModelLoader, so dependency-parser models can be loaded from streams without reflective construction.

section.title: Building an image
section.para: Add the OpenNLP modules the application needs as ordinary dependencies and build the image with the GraalVM Maven plugin or with native-image directly. Load models from files or streams:
The GraalVM JDK must be version 25 or later. The opennlp-native-tests module builds and runs its smoke test with the native profile:

section.title: Custom extensions
section.para: A custom factory, serializer, feature generator or trainer that a model or a descriptor refers to by class name must be registered, because the image contains no reflection metadata for it. Implement ExtensionRegistrar in the jar that ships the extension and list it in META-INF/services/opennlp.tools.util.ext.ExtensionRegistrar:

An application can also register its extensions at startup through ExtensionRegistry.getDefault(). A registered extension needs no allowlist entry and no reflection metadata, on the JVM as well as in the image.

listitem.para: Class path scanning for models (SimpleClassPathModelFinder, ClassgraphModelFinder) is not available. The simple finder logs a warning and returns an empty result in an image. Load models from files or streams, or bundle them as resources and register the resource names in the application's own metadata.

Java serialization of models is not supported. BaseModel.deserialize and the SvmDoccatModel persistence methods throw an UnsupportedOperationException in an image. Use the model's own format, that is serialize(OutputStream) and the InputStream constructor.
opennlp-dl and the ONNX Runtime are out of scope, as is the opennlp-cli module, because its argument parser builds interface proxies.

Unregistered extension classes named in a model can still be loaded reflectively on the JVM, behind the package allowlist described in . In an image that path only works with reflection metadata provided by the application; registering the extension is the supported way.
